 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 25-08-2023 at about 11-00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-K-7088 from Udayapura Town- Kundur main road and when he reached near Yaliyur village Dandiganahalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk,
Hassan District, at that time the driver of Maruthi Goods Carrier vehicle bearing No.KA-18-C-9177 came suddenly from Udayapura side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The petitioner was shifted to Govt Hospital at Channarayapattna wherein first aid treatment was given and he was referred for higher treatment at Punya Hospital at Channarayapattna and then he was shifted to Government Hospital at Hassan wherein admitted as an inpatient for one month.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He has aged about 19 years.
The petitioner was agriculturist and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non- pecuniary damages.
4. On service of notice, the Respondent no.1 has appeared through his counsel but has not filed written statement and thereby uncontested the petition 5.
The Respondent no.2/

the insurer of Maruthi Goods Carrier vehicle bearing No.KA-18-C-9177 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that there is an inordinate delay on the part of claimant in filing the claim petition, that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident, that the petitioner, in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gains and that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving licence and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

The respondent no.2 further contended that as per the police documents,
the petitioner being a minor without holding driving licence was riding the motorcycle.
Hence petitioner too has contributed negligence.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, on 25-08-2023 at about 11-00 pm., he was proceeding in Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06- K-7088 on the left side of the road near Yaliyur village, Udayapura to Kundur matta road,
Dandiganahalli Hobli, Channarayapattana Taluk, at that time, the driver of Maruthi Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-18-C-9177 suddenly came from Udayapura side in a rash or negligent manner and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3

. What order or Award ?
8.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 to PW.4 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.

The respondent no.2 has examined its Asst.Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
9.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle,
the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 25-08-2023 at about 11- 00 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-K-7088 from Udayapura Town- Kundur main road and when he reached near Yaliyur village Dandiganahalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, at that time the driver of Maruthi Goods Carrier vehicle bearing No.KA-18-C-9177 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came suddenly from Udayapura side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with Complaint, Crime details form, spot sketch, seizer mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, etc.,

sentences.text: On the basis of the complaint lodged by Kumari, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0134/2023 by Channarayapatna Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
13.

As observed supra, the respondent no.2 has taken the contention that at time of accident the petitioner was minor aged about 17 years 2 months and 2 days and that since he was minor, he was not holding driving licence and that accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle by the petitioner.
It is relevant to state here that the respondent no.2 has not seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The accident in question has occurred on 25.08.2023 at about 11.00 p.m.
The complaint came to be lodged on the same date.
In the complaint the registration number of the offending vehicle and the name of the driver of the offending vehicle is also mentioned.
Further as per the IMV report, damage was caused even to the offending vehicle.
Hence involvement of offending vehicle is proved by the petitioner.
14. The petitioner in his petition has contended that at the time of accident he was major and he was holding valid driving licence.
Even in the evidence also the petitioner has deposed so.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card as per Ex.P8.

The petitioner while admitting that in the Aadhar card his date of birth is mentioned as 23.06.2006 has deposed that even though his date of birth is mentioned as 23 .06.2006 in the Aadhar card but his date birth is 23.06.2003, hence as on the date of accident he was major.
As per the evidence of petitioner, he has studied ITI.

If really the date of birth of petitioner is 23.06.2003 and if really his date of birth is wrongly mentioned in the Aadhar card as 23.06.2006, then nothing prevented the petitioner from producing his school records to prove his date of birth as 23.06.2003 and thereby to prove that he was major as on the date of accident.
It is relevant to state here that the petitioner during his further cross examination has admitted that at the time of accident he was aged about 17 years 2 months and 2 days.
Hence it can be said that as on the date of accident the petitioner was minor and since he was minor, he was not holding driving licence.

But the mere fact that petitioner was minor and he was not holding driving licence on that ground alone court cannot attribute negligence on the petitioner unless it is proved as to how he has contributed negligence in causing the accident.

15. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, in the complaint, in the FIR, in the charge sheet and in the petition it is stated that at the time of accident the petitioner was proceeding in his motor cycle from Udayapura towards Huliyuru and offending vehicle which came from Udayapura side hit to the motor cycle of the petitioner.

Though the petitioner in specific terms, has not stated that the offending vehicle has hit to the motor cycle from behind but if offending vehicle came from Udayapura side and when petitioner was also proceeding from Udayapura side towards Huliyuru side then the offending vehicle has to hit towards the rear side of the motor cycle.
If the IMV report is perused the front right side door of the offending vehicle was dented and scratched and front wheel mud guard of the motor cycle was dented.
Further the front head light assembly was damaged with other damages.

sentences.text: Though in all the documents including the petition it was stated that both the petitioner and offending vehicle was proceeding on the same direction but the PW.1 in his cross examination has deposed that at the time of accident he was proceeding from Udayapura towards Yadiyuru and that the said road was a single road and there is a curve near Yadiyuru and that offending vehicle which came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner in a curve road dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner.

It was the suggestion posed to the PW.1 that the driver of the offending vehicle by blowing horn was driving the vehicle in the curve road but the petitioner by driving his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner hit to the offending vehicle.
The petitioner has produced spot mahazar and sketch at Ex.P2 and Ex.P3.
Since the print of the Ex.P2 was not properly taken, the writings in the Ex.P2 is not legible.
If the spot mahazar is perused it is no where stated the direction in which the petitioner's vehicle and the offending vehicle was moving at the time of accident.

Hence as there is no clarity in the pleadings and evidence regarding the direction in which the offending vehicle was proceeding and the way in which accident in question has occurred and since counsel for petitioner has not clarified the said ambiguity, this court holds that petitioner has contributed negligence to an extent of 15% by relying upon his evidence coupled with the sketch as in the sketch the spot of accident is shown on the right side of Udayapura Huliyuru road.
Hence the petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and medical bills which are marked at Ex.P6 and 9.
If bill as per Ex.P9 issued from Punya Hospital is perused wherein the date of admission and date of discharge is shown as 25.08.2023.
It means the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient only for 1 day at Punya Hospital.

If Ex.P16 is perused i.e.,
summary sheet maintained in Hassan Institute of Medical Science Teaching is perused, it discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 27.08.2023 to 01.09.2023.

entities.text: Hassan Institute of Medical Science Teaching
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It means the petitioner has taken treatment in all for a period of 6 days as an inpatient.

If wound certificate at Ex.P6 and the medical documents pertaining to General Hospital Channarayapatna and Hassan Institute of Medical Science Teaching Hospital is perused, the petitioner has sustained injury on his right eye, for which he has taken treatment.

entities.text: Hassan Institute of Medical Science Teaching Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained three injuries of which injury no.1 and 2 are simple in nature and injury no.3 is grievous in nature.

18. Jagadish - Hassan Institute of Medical Science, Hassan, is examined as PW2 and through him case sheet, out patient record, MLC and X-ray films are marked as Ex.P.16 and 19.
19.

entities.text: Hassan Institute of Medical Science, Hassan
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Dr.Prathap V G.M., Senior Resident, Department of Ophthalmology, Hassan, is examined as PW3.

The PW.3 has deposed that he treated the petitioner at casualty for multiple injuries to right knee, right shoulder and right sided periorbital edeama with superficial laceration over right eye brow and admitted with IP No.20233965.

PW.3 further deposed that the petitioner has taken follow up treatment on 16-08-2025 in consulted Department of Ophthalmology, HIMS, Hassan and was reviewed, he had decreased in the visual activity in the right eye 6/60 and was unable to identify the colours properly on dilated fundus examination, he had optic disc pallar (partial optic atrophy) in the right side probably be caused by trauma or injuries.

sentences.text: If the evidence of PW.3 is perused on 16.08.2025 alone he has given treatment to the petitioner at OPD.
Prior to that the petitioner had taken treatment in their hospital but the causality doctor had given treatment to the petitioner.
The PW.3 has deposed in his examination chief that the petitioner had decreased in the visual activity in the right eye 6/60 and was unable to identify the colors properly.
But he has not assessed the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner.
No where in the evidence in chief, the PW.3 has stated in specific terms the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner.

During the cross examination, the PW.3 has deposed that as per the Government guidelines, if any person has defect of 6/60 visual activities, the disability at the rate of 10 to 15% can be considered.
But as PW.3 has not assessed the disability of the petitioner in particular, there is no ground to consider that the petitioner has suffered any percentage of disability.
21. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
22. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury and two simple injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
23. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, he has produced medical bill for Rs.27,727/- as per Ex.P.9.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.27,727/- under the head medical expenses.
24. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 19 years and he was an Agriculturist and Hotel business and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.
25. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has examined its Asst. Manager as RW.1.
The RW.1 has deposed that petitioner was student and was aged about 17 years 2 months 2 days as on the date of accident.

26. The petitioner has produced Aadhaar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 23-06- 2006 and as the accident took place in the year 2023, therefore the deceased was aged about 17 years 2 months 2 days as on the date of accident.
27.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
28.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 6 days as an inpatient in Punya Diagnostic center and Govt. Hospital, Hassan.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which are simple and grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down Akasha Y G vs Prakasha C S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117268981/
6 period as Rs.16,000/- p.m. for two months.

entities.text: Akasha Y G vs Prakasha C S
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.32,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid down period .
29. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 6 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2023.
30. As observed supra as per the evidence of PW.3, the petitioner had decreased in the visual activity in the right eye 6/60 and is unable to identify the colors properly.

Hence, this court is of the opinion that petitioner though not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income but is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort on little higher side.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.N Heads Amount o.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs. 27,727/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 32,000/-
 laid up period

4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5. Discomfort and amenities Rs.1,00,000/-
 Total Rs.2,54,727/-
Therefore

this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,54,727/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Four Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty Seven only).
32.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the rider of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both petitioner and respondent no.2 had contributed negligence to the extent of 85:15 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
The respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to pay 85% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
85% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
31. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

sentences.text: The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,54,727/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Four Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty Seven only).

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 85% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.2,16,518/-
(Rupees Two Lakhs Sixteen Thousand Five Hundred Eighteen only) with interest at 6% pa., within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.2,16,518/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 15% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.38,209/-.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
